basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Qui egrediebatur et revertebatur, donec siccarentur aquae super terram. Non ait egressus'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Qui egrediebatur et revertebatur, donec siccarentur aquae super terram. Non ait egressus est et reversus est in arcam; sed egrediebatur, inquit, et revertebatur donec siccarentur aquae super terram, quia videlicet huc illucque volatu dubio vertebatur, modo abire incipiens, modo ad arcam velut intraturus rediens, nec tamen fenestram unde egressus fuerat repetens, sed potius foris vagans usque dum remotis aquis requiem sibi ac sedem extra arcam reperiret; cujus egressui atque itineri recte comparantur hi qui sacramentis quidem coelestibus instituti atque imbuti sunt, nec tamen nigredinem terrenae oblectationis exuentes, lata potius mundi itinera quam ecclesiasticae conversationis claustra diligunt.
